arxiv-1505-01695.title: Proving Termination of Graph Transformation Systems using Weighted Type Graphs over Semirings Thanks: Research partially supported by DFG project GaReV .
arxiv-1505-01695.creator: H.J. Sander Bruggink, Barbara König, Dennis Nolte, Hans Zantema
arxiv-1505-01695.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by H.J. Sander Bruggink, Barbara König, Dennis Nolte, Hans Zantema. We introduce techniques for proving uniform termination of graph transformation systems, based on matrix interpretations for string rewriting. We generalize this technique by adapting it to graph rewriting instead of string rewriting and by generalizing to ordered semirings. In this way we obtain a framework which is inspired by the tropical and arctic type graphs of [ 5 ] and introduces a new variant of arithmetic type graphs.

arxiv-2006-03351.title: Extracting Spatiotemporal Demand for Public Transit from Mobility Data
arxiv-2006-03351.creator: Trivik Verma*, Mikhail Sirenko, Itto Kornecki, Scott Cunningham, Nuno A. M. Araújo
arxiv-2006-03351.description: Abstract With people constantly migrating to different urban areas, our mobility needs for work, services and leisure are transforming rapidly. The changing urban demographics pose several challenges for the efficient management of transit services. To forecast transit demand, planners often resort to sociological investigations or modelling that are either difficult to obtain, inaccurate or outdated.

arxiv-2110-02419.title: Feature Selection by a Mechanism Design Thanks: The views expressed herein are those of the author and should not be attributed to the IMF, its Executive Board, or its management. Affiliation: International Monetary Fund
arxiv-2110-02419.creator: Xingwei Hu
arxiv-2110-02419.description: Abstract In constructing an econometric or statistical model, we pick relevant features or variables from many candidates. A coalitional game is set up to study the selection problem where the players are the candidates and the payoff function is a performance measurement in all possible modeling scenarios.

arxiv-2111-00544.title: On black hole supertranslations and hydrodynamic enstrophy
arxiv-2111-00544.creator: Raja Marjieh, Natalia Pinzani-Fokeeva, Bar Tavor, Amos Yarom
arxiv-2111-00544.description: Abstract We study the relation between approximate horizon symmetries of AdS black branes and approximately conserved currents in their dual hydrodynamic description. We argue that the existence of an approximately conserved enstrophy current unique to 2 + 1 2+1 dimensional fluid flow implies that AdS 4 black branes possess a special class of approximate supertranslations (which we identify).

arxiv-2112-14278.title: β \beta -VAE Reproducibility: Challenges and Extensions
arxiv-2112-14278.description: Abstract β \beta -VAE is a follow-up technique to variational autoencoders that proposes special weighting of the KL divergence term in the VAE loss to obtain disentangled representations. Unsupervised learning is known to be brittle even on toy datasets and a meaningful, mathematically precise definition of disentanglement remains difficult to find.

arxiv-2202-09456.title: From Hesitancy Framings to Vaccine Hesitancy Profiles: A Journey of Stance, Ontological Commitments and Moral Foundations
arxiv-2202-09456.creator: Maxwell Weinzierl, Sanda Harabagiu
arxiv-2202-09456.description: Abstract While billions of COVID-19 vaccines have been administered, too many people remain hesitant. Twitter, with its substantial reach and daily exposure, is an excellent resource for examining how people frame their vaccine hesitancy and to uncover vaccine hesitancy profiles.

arxiv-2303-13860.title: Generalized Sparse Regression Codes for Short Block Lengths
arxiv-2303-13860.creator: Madhusudan Kumar Sinha 1 , Arun Pachai Kannu 2
arxiv-2303-13860.description: Abstract Sparse regression codes (SPARC) connect the sparse signal recovery framework of compressive sensing with error control coding techniques. SPARC encoding produces codewords which are sparse linear combinations of columns of a dictionary matrix. SPARC decoding is accomplished using sparse signal recovery algorithms.

arxiv-2311-18091.title: Relaxation in dipolar spin ladders: from pair production to false-vacuum decay
arxiv-2311-18091.creator: Gustavo A. Domínguez-Castro, Thomas Bilitewski, David Wellnitz, Ana Maria Rey, Luis Santos
arxiv-2311-18091.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gustavo A. Domínguez-Castro, Thomas Bilitewski, David Wellnitz, Ana Maria Rey, Luis Santos. Ultracold dipolar particles pinned in optical lattices or tweezers provide an excellent platform for the study of the intriguing equilibration dynamics of spin models with dipolar exchange. Starting with an initial state in which spins of opposite orientation are prepared in each of the legs of a ladder lattice, we show that spin relaxation displays an unexpected dependence on inter-leg distance and dipole orientation.

arxiv-2312-07632.title: Maximizing Social Welfare in Score-Based Social Distance Games
arxiv-2312-07632.creator: Robert Ganian, Thekla Hamm, Dušan Knop, Sanjukta Roy, Šimon Schierreich, Ondřej Suchý
arxiv-2312-07632.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Robert Ganian, Thekla Hamm, Dušan Knop, Sanjukta Roy, Šimon Schierreich, Ondřej Suchý. Social distance games have been extensively studied as a coalition formation model where the utilities of agents in each coalition were captured using a utility function u u that took into account distances in a given social network.

arxiv-2403-01217.title: The origin of lopsided satellite galaxy distribution around isolated systems in MillenniumTNG
arxiv-2403-01217.creator: Yikai Liu, Peng Wang, Hong Guo, Volker Springel, Sownak Bose, Rüdiger Pakmor, Lars Hernquist
arxiv-2403-01217.description: Abstract Dwarf satellites in galaxy groups are distributed in an anisotropic and asymmetric manner, which is called the “lopsided satellite distribution”. This lopsided signal has been observed not only in galaxy pairs but also in isolated systems. However, the physical origin of the lopsided signal in isolated systems is still unknown.

arxiv-2406-13237.title: ModelMix: A New Model-Mixup Strategy to Minimize Vicinal Risk across Tasks for Few-scribble based Cardiac Segmentation
arxiv-2406-13237.creator: Ke Zhang, Vishal M. Patel
arxiv-2406-13237.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ke Zhang, Vishal M. Patel. Pixel-level dense labeling is both resource-intensive and time-consuming, whereas weak labels such as scribble present a more feasible alternative to full annotations. However, training segmentation networks with weak supervision from scribbles remains challenging. Inspired by the fact that different segmentation tasks can be correlated with each other, we introduce a new approach to few-scribble supervised segmentation based on model parameter interpolation, termed as ModelMix .

arxiv-2407-03538.title: Exotic and physics-informed support vector machines for high energy physics
arxiv-2407-03538.creator: A. Ramirez-Morales, A. Gutiérrez-Rodríguez, T. Cisneros-Pérez, H. Garcia-Tecocoatzi, A. Dávila-Rivera
arxiv-2407-03538.description: Abstract In this article, we explore machine learning techniques using support vector machines with two novel approaches: exotic and physics-informed support vector machines. Exotic support vector machines employ unconventional techniques such as genetic algorithms and boosting. Physics-informed support vector machines integrate the physics dynamics of a given high-energy physics process in a straightforward manner.

arxiv-2408-15466.title: HUPD-2406 B ( s ) → D ( s ) ( ∗ ) ​ M B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M decays in the presence of final-state interaction
arxiv-2408-15466.creator: Albertus Hariwangsa Panuluh 1,2 , Satoshi Tanaka 3 , Hiroyuki Umeeda 4,5,6 1 Department of Physics Education, Faculty of Teacher Training and Education, Sanata Dharma University, Paingan, Maguwohardjo, Sleman, Yogyakarta 55282, Indonesia 2 Physics Program, Graduate School of Advanced Science and Eng
arxiv-2408-15466.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Decays of B mesons played an important role in testing the standard model (SM), as well as possible new physics (NP) contributions. Of the specific decay modes, nonleptonic channels are rather challenging processes in the context of strong interactions.

arxiv-2411-12564.title: CHANG-ES XXXV: Cosmic Ray Transport and Magnetic Field Structure of NGC 3556 at 3 GHz
arxiv-2411-12564.creator: Jianghui Xu, Yang Yang, Jiang-Tao Li, Guilin Liu, Judith Irwin, Ralf-Jürgen Dettmar, Michael Stein, Theresa Wiegert, Q. Daniel Wang, Jayanne English
arxiv-2411-12564.description: Abstract Radio halos of edge-on galaxies are crucial for investigating cosmic ray propagation and magnetic field structures in galactic environments. We present VLA C-configuration S-band (2–4 GHz) observations of the spiral galaxy NGC 3556, a target from the Continuum Halos in Nearby Galaxies - an EVLA Survey (CHANG-ES).

arxiv-2505-23816.title: A Course Correction in Steerability Evaluation: Revealing Miscalibration and Side Effects in LLMs
arxiv-2505-23816.creator: Trenton Chang, Tobias Schnabel, Adith Swaminathan, Jenna Wiens
arxiv-2505-23816.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Trenton Chang, Tobias Schnabel, Adith Swaminathan, Jenna Wiens. Despite advances in large language models (LLMs) on reasoning and instruction-following tasks, it is unclear whether they can reliably produce outputs aligned with a variety of user goals, a concept called steerability .

arxiv-2507-20176.title: Post-Hopf group algebras, Hopf group braces and Rota-Baxter operators on Hopf group algebras
arxiv-2507-20176.creator: Yan Ning, Xing Wang, Daowei Lu
arxiv-2507-20176.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we introduce the notions of Hopf group braces, post-Hopf group algebras and Rota-Baxter Hopf group algebras as important generalizations of Hopf brace, post Hopf algebra and Rota-Baxter Hopf algebras respectively. We also discuss their relationships.

arxiv-2604-10001.creator: Akihito Kato, Nobuhiko Yokoshi

europmc-pmc4569729.title: The links between ecosystem multifunctionality and above- and belowground biodiversity are mediated by climate.
europmc-pmc4569729.creator: Jing X, Sanders NJ, Shi Y, Chu H, Classen AT, Zhao K, Chen L, Shi Y, Jiang Y, He JS.
europmc-pmc4569729.description: Plant biodiversity is often correlated with ecosystem functioning in terrestrial ecosystems. However, we know little about the relative and combined effects of above- and belowground biodiversity on multiple ecosystem functions (for example, ecosystem multifunctionality, EMF) or

pmc-10641076.title: Engineering the structural and electrical interplay of nanostructured Au resistive switching networks by controlling the forming process
pmc-10641076.creator: Giacomo Nadalini, Francesca Borghi, Tereza Košutová, Andrea Falqui, Nicola Ludwig, Paolo Milani
pmc-10641076.description: Networks of random-assembled gold clusters produced in the gas phase show resistive switching (RS) activity at room temperature and they are suitable for the fabrication of devices for neuromorphic data processing and classification. Fully connected cluster-assembled nanostructured Au films are characterized by a granular structure rich of interfaces, grain boundaries and crystalline defects.

pmc-10751535.title: Pre-existing neurological conditions and COVID-19 co-infection: Data from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and scoping reviews
pmc-10751535.creator: Abhilasha P Boruah, Kiran T Thakur, Sachin P Gadani, Kavita U Kothari, Mashina Chomba, Alla Guekht, Kimia Heydari, Fan Kee Hoo, Soonmyung Hwang, Benedict D Michael, Maya V Pandit, Carlos A Pardo, Kameshwar Prasad, Zomer Sardar, Katrin Seeher, Tom Solomon, Andrea S Winkler, Greta K Wood, Nicoline Sch
pmc-10751535.description: BackgroundPre-existing neurological diseases have been identified as risk factors for severe COVID-19 infection and death. There is a lack of comprehensive literature review assessing the relationship between pre-existing neurological conditions and COVID-19 outcomes. Identification of high risk groups is critical for optimal treatment and care.

pmc-11590399.title: miR-122/NEGR1 axis contributes colorectal cancer liver metastasis by PI3K/AKT pathway and macrophage modulation
pmc-11590399.creator: Shipeng Dai, Haiwen Zhuang, Zhuozheng Li, Zhongda Chen, Yue Chai, Qing Zhou
pmc-11590399.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a prevalent malignant tumor in the gastrointestinal tract, with around 50% of patients experiencing distant metastases, predominantly to the liver. Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) is a leading cause of CRC-related death, and effective treatments remain limited. This study aims to identify new targets for predicting and treating CRLM.

pmc-11592443.title: A Pathological Assessment of the Microvasculature of Biliary Tract Neoplasms Referring to Pre-Existing Blood Vessels and Vessel Co-Option
pmc-11592443.creator: Yasuni Nakanuma, Zihan Li, Yasunori Sato, Motoko Sasaki, Kenichi Harada, Yuko Kakuda, Takashi Sugino, David Wong
pmc-11592443.description: Simple SummaryIn large bile ducts, the biliary lining epithelia and underlining capillaries (peribiliary capillary plexus [PCP]) form the biliary epithelia–PCP alignment, whereas the hepatocyte–sinusoid alignment composes hepatic lobules. High-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasm (BilIN) and intraductal papillary neoplasm (IPNB), and intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPN) have recently been proposed as the precursors of biliary tract carcinoma (BTC).

pmc-12506184.title: Robust myocardium detection and scar severity classification in LGE-CMR using ScarYOLO and contrastive learning
pmc-12506184.creator: B. Abinaya, M. Malleswaran, V. Muthupriya
pmc-12506184.description: Late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) imaging plays a crucial role in assessing myocardial scar tissues, aiding in the diagnosis and prognosis of cardiovascular diseases. However, accurately classifying scar tissue severity into mild and severe remains a challenge due to low contrast, noise interference, and inter-patient variability in LGE-CMR images.

pmc-12572954.title: Implant Renal Injury‐Responsive Cells to Supplement Erythropoietin and Protect Kidney Injury
pmc-12572954.creator: Hao Nie, Chen Liang, Yingxin He, Siyu Wang, Xiaopeng Zhang, Jun Duan, Jieli Huang, Chen Yu, Yujia Wang, Zixian Zhao, Wei Zuo, Ting Zhang
pmc-12572954.description: Anemia poses a life‐threatening risk to individuals with chronic kidney diseases (CKDs). Insufficient production of erythropoietin (EPO) from the injured kidney is the major reason for anemia, while lack of EPO would further aggravate the kidney injury and make a “vicious cycle.

pmc-12722416.title: Repeated Levonorgestrel Administration Impairs Cognitive Function via Glutamatergic Transmission and CaMKII–PKA–BDNF Signaling in the Hippocampus of Female Wistar Rats
pmc-12722416.creator: Halimat Amin Abdulrahim, Noah Adavize Omeiza, Ganiu Jimoh Akorede, Oluwadamilare Iyapo, John Olabode Fatoki, Ben-Azu Benneth, Emmanuel Bukoye Oyewo, Aboyeji Lukuman Oyewole, Abdullateef Isiaka Alagbonsi, Adeniran Sanmi Adekunle
pmc-12722416.description: BackgroundLevonorgestrel (LNG), a synthetic progestin widely used in emergency contraception, is increasingly taken frequently and often without medical supervision. With rising concerns that repeated exposure to such hormones may adversely affect brain function, this study investigated whether chronic LNG administration impairs cognitive-like behavior and alters key neurochemical pathways in female Wistar rats.

pmc-12783718.title: Genes, shells, and AI: using computer vision to detect cryptic morphological divergence between genetically distinct populations of limpets
pmc-12783718.creator: Jack D Hollister, David A Paz-García, Rodrigo Beas-Luna, Tammy Horton, Xiaohao Cai, Phillip B Fenberg
pmc-12783718.description: Many species are composed of two or more genetically distinct clades, indicating ongoing or past evolutionary divergence. Often however, there are no obvious morphological differences between clades, making it difficult to accurately assess specific aspects of biodiversity or to enact targeted conservation efforts.

pmc-12818971.title: Blackout in Spain: Urgent Analysis of Impact on Emergency Medical Services
pmc-12818971.creator: Rafael Castro-Delgado, Youcef Azeli, Manuel Pardo Ríos, Joseph Cuthbertson, Ginés Martínez Bastida, Xavier Jiménez-Fábrega
pmc-12818971.description: On April 28, 2025, a large-scale blackout affected mainland Spain and Portugal for over ten hours, severely impacting Emergency Medical Services (EMS). Although the cause remains uncertain and initially cyberattack was a concern, it has most probably been related to infrastructure failure.

pmc-12975641.title: Assessment of Clinical Hematology Laboratory Performance Using Sigma Metrics and Associated Factors in Total Testing Process at the Dessie Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Northeast, Ethiopia: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-12975641.creator: Zewudu Mulatie, Endris Ebrahim, Mihreteab Alebachew, Alemu Gedefie, Bruktawit Eshetu, Mihret Tilahun, Habtu Debash, Yeshimebet Kassa, Ermiyas Alemayehu, Tesfaye Gessese, Dereje Mengesha Berta
pmc-12975641.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and AimsClinical laboratory test results play a fundamental role in clinical decision making, influencing approximately 70% of medical decisions. Numerous studies have shown that errors can occur throughout the total testing process. This study aimed to assess the performance of the Clinical Hematology Laboratory and identify associated factors using sigma metrics across the total testing process at Dessie Comprehensive Specialized Hospital.MethodsA cross‐sectional study was conducted from July1, 2023, to September 30, 2023.

pmc-13152184.title: Complete genome and functional insights into Microbacterium sp. strain FBCC-B4120, a novel freshwater isolate with diverse biotechnological traits
pmc-13152184.creator: Jina Kim, Hyaekang Kim, Jaeduk Goh, Chun-Zhi Jin, Hyung-Gwan Lee, Chang Soo Lee, Sanghwa Park, Eu Jin Chung, Yejin Park, Seungmin Shin, Youngmin Han, Woori Kwak
pmc-13152184.description: The genus Microbacterium encompasses a diverse group of Actinobacteria with broad ecological distribution and functional versatility. Here, we report the complete genome sequence of Microbacterium sp. FBCC-B4120, a novel strain isolated from a freshwater ecosystem in Korea. The genome was assembled into a single circular chromosome of 3.78 Mb with a G + C content of 70.

pmc-13182211.title: Prognostic Value of Small Coved‐Type ST‐Segment Area in Patients With Spontaneous Type 1 Brugada Syndrome
pmc-13182211.creator: Nario Sano, Tetsuji Shinohara, Keisuke Yonezu, Masaki Takahashi, Hirochika Yamasaki, Kei Hirota, Hidekazu Kondo, Akira Fukui, Hidefumi Akioka, Yasushi Teshima, Naohiko Takahashi
pmc-13182211.description: BackgroundRisk stratification in Brugada syndrome (BrS) remains challenging. Although spontaneous Type 1 ECG and clinical history (e.g., prior ventricular fibrillation [VF] or syncope) are established risk markers, additional electrocardiographic predictors are needed to refine prognostication.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 82 consecutive BrS patients referred to Oita University Hospital.

pmc-13305371.title: Diagnostic performance of point-of-care ultrasound for pediatric skull fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13305371.creator: Xiaoyang Wang, Gaofeng Rao, Gang Yang, Yangtian Ye, Xiaoshuang Jiang, Jiuzhou Lin, Min Tang, Lihui Chen, Liuxian Pan, Weiting Chen, Xianlong Wu

pmc-13357170.title: Autonomic nervous system: an integrative regulator in circadian rhythm of blood pressure
pmc-13357170.creator: Zhongyang Yu, Meng Zhao, Hongyue Xu, Ji Sun, Xiaoxing Jin
pmc-13357170.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Circadian rhythms, fundamental biological oscillations aligning physiological functions with the Earth’s 24-h cycle, profoundly influence blood pressure (BP) regulation. In this review, we first consolidates current understanding the systemic and cellular organizations of circadian clocks. Next, we delve into the intricate relationship between BP and circadian rhythms, examining how environmental cues like light, sleep, and diet disrupt these rhythms, leading to BP disorders.

pmc-13427851.title: Technique and device specific diffusion-weighted imaging detected ischemic lesions and occlusion outcomes in endovascular treatment of unruptured aneurysms
pmc-13427851.creator: Rahul Raj, Jussi Numminen, Mika Niemelä, Miikka Korja
pmc-13427851.description: BackgroundThis prospective study evaluated 6-month aneurysm occlusion and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion rates following endovascular treatment of unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs). We hypothesized that complex techniques would yield better occlusion but more DWI lesions.MethodsWe conducted a single-center, prospective cohort study of consecutive patients treated for UIAs with 6-month angiographic follow-up.

pmc-13453386.title: Antimicrobial Resistance, Molecular Epidemiology, and Virulence Profiles of Hypervirulent Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates from a Tertiary Hospital in Zunyi, Southwest China, 2021–2023
pmc-13453386.creator: Meijing Shen, Xianghao Chen, Benhai Chen, Rengui Tian, Guangwu Yang, He Zha, Kaifeng Wu, Shifei Yao
pmc-13453386.description: BackgroundTo systematically analyze the drug resistance phenotype, virulence characteristics, and molecular epidemiological characteristics of hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (hv-CRKP) in Zunyi area, and to provide experimental and epidemiological evidence for clinical accurate diagnosis and treatment, rational selection of antibiotics, and prevention and control of nosocomial infection of hv-CRKP in the region.
